title: ScopeStamp
user: A solo consultant or trade business owner who needs a client to accept a specific quote, exclusions, and change history before work starts.

evidence.quote_or_summary: A freelancer built one proposal-to-signature-to-invoice flow after having no visibility into proposals and manually turning accepted work into invoices.
A self-hosted Invoice Ninja user asks for clients to select offered products, request a quote, and generate/pay an invoice in the existing client portal.

recurrence: Two independent 2026 requests describe the quote-to-commitment gap; it is high severity because unrecorded scope and acceptance turn into unpaid disputes.
current_workaround: Emailing PDFs, accepting a reply or e-signature in another product, then copying accepted line items into an invoice.
incumbents_and_gap: HoneyBook, Bonsai, PandaDoc, and Invoice Ninja cover broad proposals and invoicing; the gap is a tiny, local acceptance packet that preserves the exact scope, exclusions, and later change approvals without becoming a CRM.
smallest_useful_product: Offline-first web app that produces a signed, shareable quote page/PDF, records explicit accept/decline and scoped change cards, and exports a compact acceptance archive. Non-goals: payment processing, lead CRM, proposal analytics, or generated legal terms.
success_measure: In a 30-day pilot, 70% of sent quotes receive an unambiguous recorded decision and every accepted job has an exportable scope record.
monetization: one-time — a self-contained records tool is more credible without a subscription tied to the user's client data.
constraints: Use tamper-evident event hashes and clear timestamp provenance; do not claim an e-signature has a particular legal effect; keep client data locally by default.
why_distinct: It is an acceptance and scope-evidence record, not another proposal template library or all-in-one freelancer suite.

title: Release Ledger
user: A freelancer or small service shop taking deposits who needs to know what has been prepaid, what work may be released, and what remains payable.

evidence.quote_or_summary: A freelancer describes final handoff as the most stressful lifecycle point and built a delivery gate to avoid sending files then hoping for payment.
A feature request says professional-services and trades clients commonly prepay deposits or retainers and reports that a payment is converted into unapplied credit.

recurrence: Two independent 2026 discussions connect deposits to delivery/release risk; a wrong balance directly creates either withheld work or accidental over-release.
current_workaround: Label deposits in a spreadsheet or invoice notes, manually subtract them later, and decide by memory whether to release the final work.
incumbents_and_gap: Stripe Invoicing, QuickBooks, and Invoice Ninja model payments, but small operators still need a plain-language per-job release ledger separate from a full accounting system.
smallest_useful_product: Local job ledger with deposit, milestone, release, refund, and balance events; a client-facing receipt; and a red/amber/green release status. Non-goals: holding funds, charging cards, collections, or accounting-ledger replacement.
success_measure: At least 90% of pilot jobs with a deposit have a recorded release decision and no job is released with an unrecorded balance after 60 days.
monetization: one-time — the value is durable local job records, not transaction volume.
constraints: Never custody money or imply escrow; configurable currency/tax labels; export CSV/PDF; protect client contact data on-device.
why_distinct: It answers 'may I release this job?' from a lightweight audit trail rather than trying to be invoicing software.

title: Party Map
user: A small agency or subcontractor that bills one client while delivering to that client's end customer and needs the relationships kept straight job by job.

evidence.quote_or_summary: An Ask HN author validating an admin app lists invoicing, purchases, inventory, and expenses; their first small-business user tracks inventory and sends quotes and invoices.
A feature request explicitly asks for an end-client/sub-client relationship across clients, projects, tasks, and invoices for subcontracted work.

recurrence: A 2025 small-business admin workflow and a 2026 dedicated sub-client feature request show the same context is missing from broad bookkeeping records.
current_workaround: Encode end-customer names in job titles, duplicate contacts, or maintain a separate spreadsheet beside the invoicing tool.
incumbents_and_gap: Jobber, ServiceM8, QuickBooks, and Invoice Ninja support clients/projects at different depths; the gap is a portable, minimal map of contracting party, delivery party, payer, and job contacts.
smallest_useful_product: Local-first job/contact graph with role labels, per-job notes, safe contact-sheet export, and invoice-reference fields. Non-goals: CRM pipeline, payroll, multi-company accounting, or payment collection.
success_measure: In pilot use, 95% of active subcontract jobs show a named payer, end client, and delivery contact without duplicated contact entries.
monetization: one-time — agencies need a small portable operational record rather than another seat-based system.
constraints: Personal data minimization, encrypted local backup, role-based redaction in exports, and no legal determination of contractual responsibility.
why_distinct: The core artifact is the relationship map, not a generic contact database or project manager.

title: DueCase
user: A freelancer who needs to follow up on an overdue invoice consistently while retaining a factual record of what was sent and what is legally safe to say.

evidence.quote_or_summary: A freelancer says they were tired of writing friendly reminder emails and built adaptive reminders around each client's payment behavior.
An Invoice Ninja user reports that the late-fee behaviour is not compliant with European law, exposing the jurisdiction-specific risk in automatic collection flows.

recurrence: Two independent requests in 2025–26 show both frequent chasing work and the compliance hazard of automatic late-payment behaviour.
current_workaround: Search sent mail, reuse an informal template, add late fees manually, or rely on a broad invoicing product's automatic sequence.
incumbents_and_gap: Chaser, Xero, QuickBooks, and Invoice Ninja automate reminders; the unresolved small-business need is a local, review-before-send case file with a jurisdiction-specific policy checklist.
smallest_useful_product: Offline case file per invoice: reminder timeline, editable plain-language templates, promised-payment log, attachments, and a pre-send policy checklist. Non-goals: sending email, debt collection, legal advice, fee calculation, or credit reporting.
success_measure: Pilot users record every follow-up in one case file and reduce time spent reconstructing an overdue-invoice history to under five minutes.
monetization: one-time — records and templates are useful without taking a percentage of recovered money.
constraints: Prominent jurisdiction/legal-advice disclaimer; no automated threats or fees; local encryption; user must approve all exported messages.
why_distinct: It is evidence and safe process support, specifically not a thin automated-reminder wrapper.

title: Move Confirmed
user: A one-person appointment business that must make cancellations and reschedules visible to customers without adopting a full vertical CRM.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Ask HN asks how small businesses handle appointment reminders; a response identifies cancellation and reschedule state management as the real problem rather than initial alerts.
The booking-system issue says staff reschedules update the diary but produce no customer notification across modal, drag-and-drop, and approval paths.

recurrence: Two independent 2026 threads identify reschedule state, not reminder delivery, as the failure point; missed moves lead directly to no-shows and customer distrust.
current_workaround: Change the calendar then text manually, rely on an automation, or hope a platform detects every editing path.
incumbents_and_gap: Calendly, Square Appointments, Fresha, and vertical CRMs offer reminders, but the gap is a lightweight proof-of-change card that works with an existing calendar.
smallest_useful_product: PWA that imports or accepts a calendar event, creates a reschedule/cancel card, opens the user's SMS/email composer with a confirmation link, and records acknowledgement. Non-goals: booking marketplace, payment deposits, mass messaging, or a calendar replacement.
success_measure: In a 30-day pilot, 90% of changed appointments receive a logged notification and fewer than 5% are disputed as unannounced.
monetization: one-time — it augments a calendar already paid for rather than charging per reminder.
constraints: Calendar permissions must be least-privilege; no unsolicited messaging; protect customer phone/email data; acknowledgement links must expire.
why_distinct: The product guarantees an auditable change handoff, not generic scheduling or reminder automation.

title: Receipt Packet
user: A self-employed person preparing a tax or accountant handoff who needs each claimed expense tied to its original receipt and an exportable explanation.

evidence.quote_or_summary: The author describes paper receipts for tax deductions and expense tracking as time-consuming to enter, easy to lose, damage, or overlook.
A production issue reports that a newly scanned receipt does not display on an employee expense after an admin replaced the receipt, showing the importance of receipt-to-expense integrity.

recurrence: Independent June 2026 reports show both the intake burden and the trust problem when a receipt loses its link to an expense.
current_workaround: Take photos into a camera roll, type a spreadsheet row, email files to an accountant, or subscribe to a full expense-management service.
incumbents_and_gap: Expensify, Dext, QuickBooks, and Zoho Expense handle capture and accounting flows; the gap is a local, accountant-ready evidence packet that does not require bank access or OCR subscription.
smallest_useful_product: Offline PWA that captures/imports receipt images, records amount/date/category/claim note, hashes the original, and exports one ZIP/PDF index per period. Non-goals: OCR, bank sync, reimbursement workflow, bookkeeping, or tax calculation.
success_measure: At period end, 80% of pilot users export a complete packet with every claimed line linked to an original image.
monetization: one-time — local capture and periodic exports suit sole traders better than per-receipt SaaS pricing.
constraints: Receipts can contain personal data; encryption and explicit backup/export are required; preserve originals; no tax-deductibility claims.
why_distinct: It is an evidence binder for a handoff, not a receipt-scanning AI or corporate expense platform.

title: Runway Notes
user: An owner of a tiny shop who needs to see the next four weeks of expected cash in and out, including uncertain invoices and recurring obligations.

evidence.quote_or_summary: A builder asks ecommerce businesses and accountants how they reconcile Shopify, payment-provider, and accounting numbers and what is most frustrating.
A user asks for a monthly cash-flow forecast that shows projected balances through the month based on missed and upcoming regular payments.

recurrence: Two 2026 discussions expose a recurring visibility problem: the balances exist in several places, but the near-term consequences do not.
current_workaround: Look at bank balance, payment dashboards, and a spreadsheet separately; reconcile only after the month closes.
incumbents_and_gap: Float, QuickBooks Cash Flow Planner, Xero, and personal-finance apps are broader systems; the gap is a local, scenario-first short-horizon ledger for a business too small to maintain full forecasts.
smallest_useful_product: Local 28-day cash board for recurring bills, expected invoices, payout delays, and confidence labels; CSV import and a printable weekly view. Non-goals: bank aggregation, accounting, forecasting with ML, credit advice, or multi-user approvals.
success_measure: At least 70% of weekly pilot reviews identify a cash shortfall or safe-to-spend amount before the relevant due date.
monetization: one-time — a local planning board should remain useful without financial-data aggregation fees.
constraints: No bank credentials or investment advice; clearly separate estimates from settled transactions; local encrypted backup option.
why_distinct: It focuses on the next cash decision and uncertainty labels, not retrospective bookkeeping or a generic budget app.

title: ShelfCard
user: A tiny stock-holding business that needs to scan an item at the shelf and record a count, location, reorder note, or supplier mismatch in seconds.

evidence.quote_or_summary: A self-employed/freelancer tracker is explicitly positioned as replacing the spreadsheet for expense, income, and invoices rather than replacing an accountant.
An InvenTree user says scanning an unknown DigiKey barcode yields only a no-match error and requests create/update-from-scan behaviour.

recurrence: One 2026 request explicitly replaces spreadsheets and one 2025 inventory feature request shows scan-time friction; together they support a low-ceremony stock task rather than ERP adoption.
current_workaround: Spreadsheet tabs, hand-written shelf labels, a phone notes app, or a large inventory package that is not opened during a count.
incumbents_and_gap: Sortly, Zoho Inventory, Square, and InvenTree support inventory, but their full catalogue/POS/ERP scope is too heavy for quick shelf-side exception capture.
smallest_useful_product: Offline camera barcode scanner with a single local shelf card per SKU: last count, location, photo, supplier code, reorder threshold, and CSV import/export. Non-goals: POS, purchasing, lot traceability, accounting, or supplier scraping.
success_measure: Pilot operators record 50 stock observations in a week with a median scan-to-save time below 15 seconds.
monetization: one-time — a local small-catalogue tool should not tax every item or scan.
constraints: Use device camera only on consent; barcode databases are optional and must use compatible licences; local export is mandatory.
why_distinct: It is a shelf-side observation card, not a stripped-down clone of an inventory ERP.

title: ReceivePad
user: A micro-retailer or maker receiving small supplier orders who needs to record partial deliveries, damage, and what still needs chasing without deploying an ERP.

evidence.quote_or_summary: A local-first accounting/ERP author describes a modular desktop system aimed at factories, wholesalers, and gemstone/jewellery businesses, demonstrating the breadth a small operator is otherwise asked to adopt.
An inventory workflow explicitly treats purchase-order duplication as a separately approved, low-frequency workflow rather than ordinary create/update behaviour.

recurrence: Two 2026 inventory/accounting discussions show purchasing workflows are both necessary and easily swallowed by ERP complexity; mistakes propagate to stock and payment records.
current_workaround: Mark supplier emails, annotate a PDF order, create duplicate spreadsheets, or force receiving into a full inventory platform.
incumbents_and_gap: Odoo, ERPNext, InvenTree, and Zoho Inventory offer purchasing, but the gap is a simple local discrepancy record for an existing order regardless of where it was created.
smallest_useful_product: Offline order card with line quantities, received/short/damaged states, photos, supplier follow-up note, and CSV/PDF export. Non-goals: issuing purchase orders, vendor payment, stock valuation, approvals, or warehouse management.
success_measure: In pilots, 90% of partial or damaged deliveries have a recorded discrepancy and follow-up within one business day.
monetization: one-time — the narrow receiving workflow does not warrant a recurring ERP subscription.
constraints: Store only business contacts necessary for follow-up; preserve photo provenance; no claim that an exported record creates a supplier dispute right.
why_distinct: It starts after an order already exists and concentrates on physical receiving exceptions, not procurement software.

title: Proofbook
user: A tiny regulated or safety-conscious business that must repeat checks and show a client, inspector, or manager the supporting evidence later.

evidence.quote_or_summary: EasyCheck is presented as a response to manual coordination: recurring checklist tasks, reminders, evidence collection, audit trails, and replacing spreadsheet-managed processes.
A compliance-manager epic calls for a document readiness matrix, missing-document strip, scoped evidence storage, and role-gated attachments.

recurrence: Independent 2026 compliance workflows describe the same recurring-check/evidence/missing-item burden; failure can stop work or fail an audit.
current_workaround: Recurring calendar tasks plus folders, spreadsheet checklists, chat reminders, and assembling proof only when asked.
incumbents_and_gap: SafetyCulture, MaintainX, Process Street, and EasyCheck are broad workflow platforms; the gap is a private, template-light evidence binder for one small operating procedure.
smallest_useful_product: Offline PWA with repeatable check cards, required evidence slots, completion/sign-off timestamps, overdue view, and a read-only evidence-bundle export. Non-goals: regulated template library, certification advice, employee surveillance, or enterprise permissions.
success_measure: Within two cycles, pilots complete 85% of scheduled checks with required evidence attached before the due date.
monetization: one-time — an offline binder is valuable precisely because sensitive operational evidence need not enter a subscription service.
constraints: Do not claim compliance or provide jurisdictional advice; encryption, retention/deletion controls, and export integrity are required.
why_distinct: It is an evidence-first checklist binder, not a generic task manager or an AI compliance wrapper.

title: Closeout Kit
user: A freelance developer or web studio finishing a client engagement who needs a clear, non-secret handoff of assets, ownership, access actions, and client acknowledgement.

evidence.quote_or_summary: A Show HN author makes portable, shareable code walkthrough files with optional client-side encrypted links, reflecting demand for a handoff artifact that does not require the recipient to join a tool.
A real business handoff issue tracks repository and CMS ownership, production deployment ownership, lingering former-owner configuration, and the desired operator outcome.

recurrence: Two independent August 2026 handoff threads show both the artifact problem and the ownership/access problem; incomplete closeouts produce operational lock-in and support debt.
current_workaround: Email a zip and a loose document, send credentials in chat, maintain a checklist in a project manager, then answer follow-up access questions for months.
incumbents_and_gap: Notion, GitHub, 1Password, and project-management tools each hold a fragment; the gap is a portable closeout packet that coordinates them without storing credentials.
smallest_useful_product: Local wizard for asset list, owners, links, transfer/revoke actions, support window, and client acknowledgement; exports a static HTML/PDF packet. Non-goals: password vault, Git host, CMS migration, remote access transfer, or file hosting.
success_measure: For 80% of pilot closeouts, the client acknowledges the packet and no ownership/access follow-up is required after 14 days.
monetization: one-time — consultants can reuse it across engagements without client accounts or hosted lock-in.
constraints: Never collect passwords, API keys, or private keys; include explicit confirmation of external transfer actions; retain only local encrypted packets.
why_distinct: It is a security-conscious closeout artifact that links to systems of record rather than pretending to replace them.

title: Matchbox Ledger
user: A freelancer using an offline invoice tool or spreadsheet who needs to match a downloaded bank/payment CSV to open invoices without handing financial data to another service.

evidence.quote_or_summary: The HN discussion is explicitly about offline invoicing for freelancers; a commenter asks whether customer online payments can be integrated and pulled back into the application.
An ERPNext user requests downloadable payment-reconciliation data because reviewing unreconciled payments and invoices only on screen is difficult to verify or share.

recurrence: Two independent 2026 threads identify the boundary between invoice records and actual payments; reconciliation is difficult even in a full ERP and missing from offline tools.
current_workaround: Mark invoices paid manually, scan bank statements, export a payment dashboard, or move to a hosted accounting platform.
incumbents_and_gap: QuickBooks, Xero, Wave, and ERPNext reconcile accounts, but the gap is a tiny local matcher that accepts files from the tools a freelancer already uses.
smallest_useful_product: Offline CSV importer for invoices and transactions, deterministic/date-amount-reference match suggestions, manual confirmation, and an exportable reconciliation report. Non-goals: bank login, live bank sync, invoicing, bookkeeping, or tax filing.
success_measure: Pilot users match at least 90% of a month's invoice payments from CSV in under 20 minutes, with every manual match carrying a note.
monetization: one-time — users should not need to upload transaction history or pay an ongoing fee for periodic file matching.
constraints: All parsing stays in-browser; no bank credentials; preserve imported source files locally only on opt-in; flag but never silently merge ambiguous matches.
why_distinct: It is a local reconciliation utility for existing records, not another accounting suite or payment processor.
